Join us this Sunday to Learn How Art and Sports Collide

Secure your seat to enjoy a lively conversation on **Sunday, November 15**, with LJ Rader and Andrew Maraniss as they explore the unexpected connections between art and athletics, Rader′s creative process, and the story behind the phenomenon that has brought millions of sports fans and art lovers together.

[Learn more and register](https://fristartmuseum.org/event/art-but-make-it-sports/)

[Museum Store Weekend graphic](https://fristartmuseum.org/event/museum-store-saturday/)

### [Holiday Shopping with Purpose!](https://fristartmuseum.org/event/museum-store-saturday/)

Mark your calendar for Museum Store Weekend! On November 28–29, the Frist gift shop will host more than 40 local vendors, including local jewelers, ceramicists, authors, and artists alongside bakers and specialty food purveyors. It’s the perfect time to find unique holiday gifts for everyone on your list.

[Learn more](https://fristartmuseum.org/event/museum-store-saturday/)

### [_Beauty and Ritual: Judaica from the Jewish Museum, New York_ is now open](https://fristartmuseum.org/exhibition/beauty-and-ritual-judaica/)

Drawn from the world-renowned collection of the Jewish Museum in New York City, _Beauty and Ritual_ presents more than 130 Jewish ceremonial objects (Judaica) created from antiquity to the present. The works represent many parts of the world, from South Asia to North Africa and from Western Europe to Australia, and display a diversity of Jewish cultures. The exhibition illuminates how Jewish communities and artists have creatively adapted traditional forms of Judaica by utilizing a rich array of materials, styles, and techniques.

[Learn more](https://fristartmuseum.org/exhibition/beauty-and-ritual-judaica/)

[Graphic promoting free memberships for college students featuring two college students talking about a piece of art](https://fristartmuseum.org/explorer-membership-2/)

### [Free Memberships for Local College Students!](https://fristartmuseum.org/explorer-membership-2/)

We’re excited to now offer the [Explorer Membership](https://fristartmuseum.org/explorer-membership-2/)—our free membership level—to local undergraduate college students! Eligible students include those who attend a college or university in Davidson, Cheatham, Robertson, Rutherford, Sumner, Williamson, or Wilson Counties, as well as college students enrolled elsewhere who maintain residence in those counties. Enjoy free admission, invitations to member events, and more!

[Join today!](https://fristartmuseum.org/explorer-membership-2/)

[A drawing of men's faces abstracting like a ribbon on a black background with spheres.](https://fristartmuseum.org/article/frist-art-museum-2027-schedule-of-exhibitions/)

### [2027 Exhibition Schedule Announced!](https://fristartmuseum.org/article/frist-art-museum-2027-schedule-of-exhibitions/)

We’re excited to announce our 2027 exhibition schedule! Highlights include _The Great Mughals_, showcasing the art and culture of the Mughal court’s golden age; _Pop to Present_, celebrating American art from the 1940s to today; and _Splendor and Luxury_, featuring French Art Nouveau and Art Deco. The year also includes exhibitions devoted to M.C. Escher, Beauford Delaney, Jerry Pinkney, Jean-Michel Basquiat, Tennessee-based artists, and others.

[Learn more](https://fristartmuseum.org/article/frist-art-museum-2027-schedule-of-exhibitions/)

**Note:** The Loeb will be closed on Sunday, January 25, due to a winter weather event.

The Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center is free and open to all. The Loeb Art Center enhances and supports the College’s goals of leadership, scholarship, and integrative learning.

The Loeb achieves this through the preservation, documentation, interpretation, presentation, and development of its collections; and through a dynamic program of temporary exhibitions and educational activities aimed at diverse audiences. Art should stand “boldly forth as an educational force,” declared founder Matthew Vassar. His college was the country’s first to be founded with a gallery and teaching collection.

Posted 9/25/2026

From October 3, 2026–January 31, 2027, the exhibition _Photo-Design: Persuasion, Critique, Fantasy_ at the Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center (“The Loeb”) will show visitors how experimental photography techniques have helped envision new possibilities and picture new futures_._

## [The Art of Healing](https://www.vassar.edu/news/art-healing)

Physicians from a local hospital gathered at The Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center recently to engage in an exercise designed to help them become better doctors.

## [Loeb Awarded Grant for Founding Galleries](https://www.vassar.edu/news/loeb-awarded-grant-founding-galleries)

The Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center was awarded an Implementation Grant by the Terra Foundation for American Art to support the reinstallation of Vassar’s Hudson River School paintings, a core feature of the College’s art collection.

Posted 2/12/2026

## [New Grant for the Loeb for Important Painting Conservation](https://www.vassar.edu/news/new-grant-loeb-important-painting-conservation)

The Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center has secured a grant from the Joan Mitchell Foundation for the conservation of “Lyric,” a 1951 oil on canvas by the late American artist Joan Mitchell (1925–1992).

## [Monumental Sculptural Artwork Added to Vassar College Grounds](https://www.vassar.edu/news/monumental-sculptural-artwork-added-vassar-college-grounds)

Posted 10/13/2025

Soaring 18 feet high, seven sentinels made of weathered steel surround a female bronze figure that appears to emerge from the earth. This dynamic and awe-inducing public artwork, situated at the northwest perimeter of the campus, is Vassar College’s newest public art acquisition.

## [_Chronostasia: Select Acquisitions 2020–2025_](https://www.vassar.edu/news/chronostasia-select-acquisitions-2020-2025)

Posted 8/18/2025

This fall, the [Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center](https://www.vassar.edu/theloeb) at Vassar presents _Chronostasia: Select Acquisitions 2020–2025_, an exhibition that brings together more than sixty works acquired over the past five years.

## [Summer Art Programming, Exhibitions Announced at the Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center at Vassar](https://www.vassar.edu/news/summer-art-programming-exhibitions-announced-frances-lehman-loeb-art-center-vassar)

Posted 6/27/2025

With the arrival of summer, Vassar’s Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center is rolling out the red carpet for art lovers this season with a wide range of events and exhibitions spanning improvised performances utilizing the gestural composing language of Soundpainting to exhibitions that explore the reciprocal relationship between place and person, showcase the museum’s collection of Hudson River School art, and examine images of the body fragmented into pieces.

## [Loeb’s New Grant Launches Restoration of 17th-century Japanese Painted Screen](https://www.vassar.edu/news/loebs-new-grant-launches-restoration-17th-century-japanese-painted-screen)

The Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center was awarded funding by Tokyo-based Sumitomo Foundation toward the restoration of a 17th-century Japanese painted screen. A rarity and a cherished work in the Loeb’s Asian art collection, the screen was painted by Unkoku Toeki in the early 1600s. Its conservation will allow it to remain a popular teaching object for Art History at Vassar.

## [Family Fun at the Loeb](https://www.vassar.edu/news/events/family-fun-loeb-3)

**Nov.** **15**, **2026**, **1:00**–**2:30 p.m.**

Join us for **free** drop-in family programs on select Sundays (October 11, November 15, and December 13) this fall. Each date will feature a different hands-on art activity inspired by art on view. Activities can be modified for all ages, but are best suited for children ages 5 and up. Check our Instagram [@theloeb](https://www.instagram.com/theloeb/?hl=en) for details about the activity, or email [loebtours@vassar.edu](mailto:loebtours@vassar.edu) with questions.

This event is free and open to the public.

## [Screening of _Rollie McKenna: Life and Photography_](https://www.vassar.edu/news/events/screening-rollie-mckenna-life-and-photography)

**Nov.** **20**, **2026**, **5:00 p.m.**

Join us for an evening with documentary filmmaker Chris Kepple, whose new documentary chronicles the life and legacy of photographer Rollie McKenna (Vassar class of 1940), who was the subject of a major retrospective at the Loeb Art Center in 2024. _Life and Photography_ will appeal to audiences interested in 20th-century literature, local history, portrait photography, architecture, literary history, popular culture, queer culture, feminist culture, and poetry. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with the director.

This event is free and open to the public.

jsonLd.description: <p>ONLINE</p> <p><a href="https://ucla.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_sA3Eya_FQYezZSxv43bkKA" target="_blank" rel="noopener">RSVP</a></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Guest curators Tangimoe Clay, Gina Tawhai Matchitt, Maui Hudson, and Brent Kerehona Pukepuke-Ahitapu will discuss the historic kaitaka (finely woven Māori cloak) in the Fowler Museum’s collection and the ways Indigenous knowledge, collaborative research, and relationships with source communities can renew connections with Māori taonga.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Using the <em>kaitaka</em> as a case study, Tangimoe Clay, Gina Tawhai Matchitt, Maui Hudson, and Brent Kerehona Pukepuke-Ahitapu will address the cloak’s weaving techniques, materials, and tāniko designs, alongside the process of locating, identifying, and researching its history. The conversation will reflect on Māori approaches to stewardship, care, and ancestral bonds, highlighting how knowledge sharing and sustained community connections can strengthen relationships with ancestral treasures in international collections. </span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Tangimoe Clay (Ngāti Ngahere, Whakatōhea)</strong> is a renown weaver and businesswoman from Whakatōhea. She grew up in Ōpōtiki and as a child her first experience of harakeke (flax) was watching her Aunty caring for a pā harakeke (flax garden). Mainly self-taught, Tangimoe later attended various weaving wananga (knowledge sharing sessions). She started her business, Tangata Whenua, in 1996, a gallery and retail store in Opotiki selling the works of local and national Māori artists. TūturuMāori, Tangimoe is a strong advocate for her Whakatōhea people and Māori art. A member of TeRoopu Raranga Whatu o Aotearoa, or National Māori Weavers, Tangimoe Clay has a Bachelor of Toi Māori (Māori art) from Te Whare Wananga o Awanuiarangi. Her work is held in national and international collections, including Te Papa Tongarewa, The National Museum of New Zealand, Auckland Museum, The Metropolitan Museum in New York, and the Fowler Museum in Los Angeles.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Maui Hudson (Ngai Tamahaua, Whakatōhea)</strong> is a professor and director of the Te Kotahi Research Institute at the University of Waikato and a council member for Local Contexts. He was previously a member of the Whakatōhea Māori Trust Board and a negotiator for the Whakatōhea Treaty Settlement. He collaborates with Te Tāwharau o Te Whakatōhea on initiatives to support Whakatōhea data sovereignty, scientific partnerships, cultural revitalization, as well as responsible research and innovation.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Gina Tawhai Matchitt (Ngāti Ngahere, Whakatōhea, Ngati Rangitihi, Te Arawa)</strong> grew up in Rotorua, New Zealand and graduated with Masters of Māori visual arts from Massey University and a postgraduate diploma in museums studies from Victoria University. Matchitt co-curated <em>Uhengaparaoa, Taonga Tuku Iho</em> at the Fowler Museum and is currently a curator at Te Whare Taonga o Waikato Museum & Gallery in Hamilton, New Zealand. Her art practice explores the traditions of Te Ao Māori (the Māori world) and their place in contemporary life, often by combining customary Māori techniques, patterns, and language with contemporary materials.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Brent Kerehona Pukepuke-Ahitapu</strong> (BA, MTeach) is a passionate and dedicated educator, researcher, published author, and cultural practitioner whose work has been utilized across several arenas, both in Aotearoa/New Zealand and around the world. A former paratrooper and military police officer, he has also worked and liaised with government and non-government organizations and institutions on a range of projects (journal articles, bilingual storybooks, historical novels, and short films) focusing on cultural, historical, and legal issues. His strengths are his ability to locate, access, collate, and evaluate information from a wide range of sources; assimilate and format this information; connect and make sense of ideas, events, and their significance. He has traveled the world extensively and has recently begun working within the curatorial space, contributing to several exhibitions. One of his passions is to locate, identify, and study Māori taonga (cultural treasures) around the globe and to write historical and technical reports about them that provide cultural context, so that they can be acknowledged and displayed in a manner that respects their mauri (life essence) and mana (prestige).</span></p>

jsonLd.description: <p>IN PERSON</p> <p><a href="https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1999148992452?aff=oddtdtcreator" target="_blank" rel="noopener">RSVP</a></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Fowler Out Loud presents </span><b>readymade</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">, a Korean-American student music group at UCLA whose performances bring together Korean music, pop culture, and contemporary expression. As a nonprofit organization, readymade creates opportunities for students to connect through music while celebrating Korean heritage, fostering cross-cultural exchange, and enriching UCLA’s artistic community.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">This concert takes place in the museum’s outdoor amphitheater (unless otherwise noted). Seating is on the grassy area; we encourage you to bring whatever helps you be comfortable, such as a chair, mat, blanket, or cushion. Savor this evening under the sky with your friends and community!</span></p> <p><b>Fowler Out Loud</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> is an evening concert series that invites UCLA students from various disciplines to perform at the museum. </span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br /> </span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Graphic designed by Samantha Chen</span></p>

jsonLd.description: <p>IN PERSON</p> <p><a href="https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1999148244214?aff=oddtdtcreator" target="_blank" rel="noopener">RSVP</a></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Lilly Endowment Curator of Art and Religion Patrick A. Polk and Haitian art specialist and oungan (Vodou priest) Jean-Daniel Lafontant consider the Vodou kiosk installation in the Fowler’s Intersections gallery, tracing connections between art, religion, transformation, and resilience in Haitian Vodou traditions.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Jean-Daniel Lafontant</strong> is a distinguished oungan (Vodou priest) and a founding member of Temple Na-Ri-VéH in Haiti. He is also the founder of ANAE (1987), a prominent association based in New York City specializing in the cultural promotion of Haitian art influenced by Vodou. Additionally, he is a board member for Le Musée d’Art Haïtien and executive director of the Haitian Cultural Foundation.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Patrick A. Polk’s</strong> research interests encompass material religion and visual piety, faith and healing, popular devotion in North and Latin America, and African diasporic sacred arts. He has curated several Fowler exhibitions, including:<em> The House Was Too Small: Yoruba Sacred Arts from Africa and Beyond; Botánica Los Angeles: Latino Popular Religious Art in the City of Angels; Sinful Saints and Saintly Sinners at the Margins of the Americas; </em>and <em>Axé Bahia: The Power of Art in an Afro-Brazilian Metropolis.</em></span></p>

jsonLd.description: <p>IN PERSON</p> <p><a href="https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1999149631363?aff=oddtdtcreator" target="_blank" rel="noopener">RSVP</a></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Curator of Textiles of the Eastern Hemisphere Syona Puliady will join UCLA Dean of the School of the Arts and Architecture Lionel Popkin for a conversation on the themes underlying </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Textiles as Monument</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Field Notes from Begumpura</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">: memory, materiality, and the creation of alternative histories through contemporary art.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">By focusing on the works of Suchitra Mattai, Jagdeep Raina, Swapnaa Tamhane, and Rahee Punyashloka, Puliady and Popkin will consider how artists use textiles, speculative storytelling, archival practices, and other forms of cultural expression to challenge dominant narratives and center communities whose histories have often been overlooked. Together, they will address how contemporary South Asian artists create new forms of remembrance, belonging, and possibility through material and imagined worlds.</span></p> <p><b>Lionel Popkin</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> is the dean of the UCLA School of the Arts and Architecture and a professor of choreography in the UCLA Department of World Arts and Cultures/Dance. He previously served as the school’s associate dean for academic affairs (2021–24) and chair of the World Arts and Cultures/Dance department (2015–18). Popkin’s artistic practice engages people, objects, and media to explore hybridity, archival practices, and the complexities of representing the South Asian diaspora in North America. His performance and video artworks have been presented at leading cultural venues on four continents, and his written works have been included in scholarly journals and arts publications. He joined UCLA’s faculty in 2006 and is a resident artist at the 18th Street Arts Center.</span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br /> </span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br /> </span><b>Syona Puliady</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> is curator of textiles of the Eastern Hemisphere at the Fowler Museum. Her research focuses on histories and textiles of the Indian Ocean realm. Her work also takes her to the South Indian state of Tamil Nadu, where she collaborates with artists and garment laborers who weave their identities into the Tamil landscape of visual, sensory, and performing arts.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Photo by Elon Schoenholz</span></p>

jsonLd.description: <p>ONLINE</p> <div class="figure"><a href="https://ucla.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_ynt-WNL7S--j-OH4is_LjA" target="_blank" rel="noopener">RSVP</a></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Building on the legacy of </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Fire Kinship: Southern California Native Ecology and Art</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">, this online panel will offer a space for reflection, dialogue, and forward-looking conversation. Moderated by </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Fire Kinship</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;"> curator Daisy O’Campo Diaz, the discussion will bring together Native curators, scholars, and cultural leaders working across academia, museums, and independent curatorial practice, including Amy Lonetree, Amanda K. Wixon, Meranda Roberts, and Lina Tejeda. Together, they will address the exhibition’s themes while engaging broader questions around Native-led curatorial methodologies, community-centered practices, and Indigenous approaches to care, stewardship, and storytelling within museums. The conversation will also consider how Native-led curatorial work is reshaping institutional practices today and imagine what futures are possible beyond the life of a single exhibition. </span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br /> </span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br /> </span><b>Daisy Ocampo Diaz</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (Caxcan) is an associate professor of history at California State University, San Bernardino, and a curator whose work grows from longstanding relationships with Southern California Tribal communities. Her research explores Indigenous histories across Southern California and the U.S.-Mexico borderlands, with attention to land, memory, sovereignty, and stewardship. She curated </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Fire Kinship: Southern California Native Ecology and Art</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">, a collaborative exhibition developed with Native fire practitioners, artists, cultural leaders, and community members. Across her exhibitions, historic preservation projects, and engagement with community-based archives, she considers how kinship and relational accountability can reshape curatorial practice, creating more reciprocal relationships among museums, communities, land, and Indigenous knowledge.</span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br /> </span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br /> </span><b>Amy Lonetree </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">is an enrolled citizen of the Ho-Chunk Nation and a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Cruz. She received her Ph.D. in ethnic studies from the University of California, Berkeley; her scholarly research focuses on 20th-century Native American history, public history, Indigenous photography, and museum studies. Her publications include </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Decolonizing Museums: Representing Native America in National and Tribal Museums; </span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">and</span> <span style="font-weight: 400;">a co-authored volume, </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">People of the Big Voice: Photographs of Ho-Chunk Families by Charles Van Schaick, 1879-1942. </span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Her book on the history of Indigenous child removal, </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Soul Wounds: The Violence of Native Child Removal and Survivance, </span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">co-authored</span> <span style="font-weight: 400;">with Sandy White Hawk, will be published by the University of California Press in February 2027.</span></p> <p><b>Meranda Roberts </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">(Yerington Paiute Tribe and Chicana) is a curator, scholar, and educator specializing in Indigenous history, museum studies, and visual culture. Using Indigenous methodologies, anti-colonial pedagogy, and Indigenous feminist theory, she critically examines colonial narratives and rethinks how museums present their collections. She earned a Ph.D. in history and an M.A. in public history from UC Riverside. Her curatorial projects include </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Continuity: Cahuilla Basket Weavers and Their Legacies</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;"> at Pomona College (2024); </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Eternal Testament</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;"> at The Church in Sag Harbor, New York, named one of the world’s top 2025 art events by </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Hyperallergic; </span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">and </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Constellations of Place</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;"> at Fort Lewis College in Durango, Colorado.</span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br /> </span></p> <p><b>Lina Tejeda</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> earned her M.A. in history from California State University, San Bernardino. Her areas of focus are California Indian studies and museum studies/public history. She is passionate about working in institutions and advocating for the return of sacred cultural items to tribal nations to which they belong, and telling the true histories of the California Indian people. Tejeda is a traditional Pomo dancer and a student of her cultural heritage, including basket weaving, materials gathering, regalia making, and singing.</span><b><br /> </b><b><br /> </b><b>Amanda K. Wixon</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (Chickasaw Nation) is the associate curator of Native history and culture at the Autry Museum of the American West. She is a doctoral candidate in Native American history at University of California, Riverside and her research interests are Native American boarding school histories, Native art, and American Indian identities. She is the co-editor and contributor to the publications </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Indigenous Activism: Profiles of Native Women in Contemporary America </span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">and </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Medicine, Education, and the Arts </span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">and </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Contemporary Native America: Strong Women, Resilient Nations</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">. Her exhibitions at the Autry include </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Sherman Indian School – 100+ Years of Education and Resilience</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and </span><i><span style="font-weight: 400;">Promised Lands: California’s Unratified Treaties and Native Resilience</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400;">.</span></p> <p><i>This program is presented ## CELEBRATING MAINE’S ROLE IN AMERICAN ART

The Farnsworth Art Museum offers a nationally recognized collection of works from many of America’s greatest artists, with 20,000 square feet of gallery space and almost 16,000 works in the collection. It has one of the largest public collections of works by sculptor Louise Nevelson, while its Wyeth Center features works of N.C., Andrew and Jamie Wyeth. The National Register-listed Farnsworth Homestead; the Olson House, a National Historic Landmark; and the Gamble Center for Education complete the complex.

Admission is free Tuesday through Sunday. Explore current exhibitions and reserve your tickets online to ensure a smooth experience.

Parking is available in the Performing Arts Center deck and surface lots, and accessible parking and assistance are always available.

#### Find Something Special

Take home more than memories. Visit the Museum Shop for unique gifts and snacks to enjoy during your visit or later.

## Opportunities for All

### Learning Through Art

#### University Programs

Turn the museum into your classroom with custom tours and study sessions that link art to your course content.

#### Student Opportunities

Through student-led events, internships and volunteer roles, we connect campus life with art through leadership and hands-on learning.

#### School & Teacher Programs

We support schools statewide, offering classroom resources and tours with free bus rides to bring more art to more students.

#### Youth & Family Programs

With programs for toddlers, teenagers and adults, the Georgia Museum of Art offers engaging experiences for the entire family.

#### Community & Public Programs

All are welcome to attend film screenings, lectures, mindfulness sessions and other free, inclusive events designed to connect.

## Inspiration Starts with You

While the Georgia Museum of Art is free to visit, it isn’t free to run. It’s fueled by people like you.

[Support the Museum](https://georgiamuseum.org/supporter-form-start/)

### Shaped by History, Driven by Possibility

**From how we started to how we’re growing.**

Founded in 1945 with just 100 paintings and a bold vision, the Georgia Museum of Art has far outgrown the library basement where we started. Now, we house tens of thousands of works of art, building for generations to come.

Learn More

Close

#### Where We Began

The Georgia Museum of Art was born from a personal passion. In his 70s, retired lawyer Alfred Heber Holbrook began studying art — not as a collector, but as a curious student. Visiting museums sparked his new purpose: to bring more art to more people.

So, Holbrook began assembling a small but powerful collection of paintings in honor of his late wife. Rather than pursuing prestige, he pursued education, connection and public good. In 1945, he donated his collection to the University of Georgia, laying the foundation of what the museum has become today.

Holbrook moved to Athens, taught himself art history and became the museum’s founding director. By 1948, the museum opened to the public in the basement of the university’s library. Soon, it grew beyond its walls and expectations.

#### Where We’re Going

As a universal language, art deserves to be shared. We’re continuously expanding our reach and building our collections to ensure that everyone sees themselves reflected on our walls. Since expanding, we’ve received incredible gifts, like the Thompsons’ collection of African American art, that have helped us connect with more people.

Our work never ends because humans never stop creating art. Through new exhibitions, digital tools and educational programs that stretch across the state, we serve the public in ways they didn’t know they needed.

The Georgia Museum of Art is more than a museum. It’s a place for people to explore, connect and discover something new. We’re building a future that stays curious.

review.reviewBody: This semester I did a lot of research for the blog posts I wrote. One of my favorites, however, was getting to write about the Carter Collection. It was a moving article to write, especially as we think about current issues.

Being part of this team helped me sharpen my communication skills and taught me a lot about how much goes on behind the scenes to maintain this museum's status as a beacon of community, education and art.
Through my work as a communications intern at the museum, I gained confidence in my ability to craft compelling written pieces. I am grateful to have had the opportunity to intern at the museum.

One of the most valuable lessons I learned as a PR intern at the museum was how to write for its website in a way that made exhibitions and events feel accessible to the broader art or non-art community.
This internship has certainly expanded my knowledge of what I can do with my degree and has undoubtedly been one of the most formative experiences of my college experience thus far.
Unlike other internships, the Georgia Museum of Art offers engaging experiences to students that enhance their skills, plus the opportunity to learn something new.
Working at the Georgia Museum of Art has been such a pleasant experience. All of the UGA administration at the museum are extremely friendly and helpful.
The hands-on experience and the impact you get to make through museum and art education is incredibly rewarding. It's been such a meaningful and inspiring experience!

The most lasting impact has been the warm community I found at the museum and the lasting connections I formed. Interning with the Georgia Museum of Art this semester has been a truly invaluable experience.
Wonderful place to visit.  Nice collection of both religious and secular art!
Thank you so much to Noelle Shuck, Michael Lachowski and Hillary Brown for their patience and continued mentorship in all things communication and design!
Beautiful place to learn more about the history of art in Georgia. Admission is free.
It was an Amazing place just for all kinds of art on view for the visitors to experience.
Great place to visit. Loved the new Ukrainian exhibit.
Always a great time, especially good shows on display at the moment. Grateful that our community has this incredible and free museum.
Another UGA gem in Athens, a fantastic small art museum. we had a great visit, 2 hours should be sufficient, great job on labeling each artwork with backstory.
Excellent free museum took about 2 hours. Free admission and parking. Friendly staff.

jsonLd.description: The Georgia Museum of Art is an art museum in Athens, Georgia, United States, associated with the University of Georgia. The museum is both an academic museum and, since 1982, the official art museum of the state of Georgia.

## Help Make This All Possible. Become a Member

- ### Free Admission

 Members receive free admission to the Museum for one year and members-only pricing on the Home & Studio tours in Abiquiú.

- ### Members-Only Events

 Access to exclusive members-only events as well as a one-year subscription to O’Keeffe Magazine.

- ### Store Discounts

 Receive a 25% discount on your first store purchase and then 15% all retail purchases for the remainder of the year.

- ### A Shared Investment

 You sustain the Museum and make our work to preserve, present, and advance the artistic legacy of Georgia O’Keeffe possible.

[Become a Member](https://www.okeeffemuseum.org/join-give/)

## Research

[**Michael S. Engl Family Foundation Library and Archive**](https://www.okeeffemuseum.org/library-and-archive/)

Santa Fe, NM Visit by Appointment

The Library & Archive serves the public by collecting, providing access to, and preserving information about Georgia O’Keeffe and her contemporaries, related regional histories, and Modernism. The Research Collections and Services team is available to answer questions, share resources, and help with your research projects.

[Learn More](https://www.okeeffemuseum.org/library-and-archive/)

## Experience

# Indigenous Creativity

[Plan Your Visit](http://heard.org/plan)

## WELCOME TO THE HEARD MUSEUM

Discover the rich and vibrant world of American Indian art, from traditional artworks to contemporary creations, live events and a world-class museum shop and café located in the heart of Phoenix, Arizona.

### Current Exhibitions

- [**Twilight: Trading Posts and Creative Legacies**\\ \\ Through August 1, 2027](https://heard.org/exhibition/twilight/)
- [**Wisdom from the Future**\\ \\ Through January 3, 2027](https://heard.org/exhibition/wisdom-from-the-future/)
- [**Substance of Stars**\\ \\ Through November 19, 2026](https://heard.org/exhibition/substance-of-stars/)
- [**Away From Home: American Indian Boarding School Stories**](https://heard.org/exhibition/away-from-home-american-indian-boarding-school-stories/)
- [**Blue Bird**\\ \\ Through February 14, 2027](https://heard.org/exhibition/blue-bird/)
- [**American Indian Veterans National Memorial**](https://heard.org/exhibition/veterans-national-memorial/)
- [**The Third Dimension: Sculptural Stories in Stone and Bronze**](https://heard.org/exhibition/the-third-dimension-sculptural-stories-in-stone-and-bronze/)
- [**Majestic Figures: Contemporary Sculptures by Native American Artists**](https://heard.org/exhibition/majestic-figures/)
- [**HOME: Native People in the Southwest**](https://heard.org/exhibition/home-native-people-in-the-southwest/)
- [**Heard Museum History in the 1929 Gallery**](https://heard.org/exhibition/1929-gallery/)
- [**Highlights | Storyteller: The Photography of Jerry Jacka**](https://heard.org/exhibition/storyteller-highlights/)
- [**A Place Where We Emerge**](https://heard.org/exhibition/abeyta-mural/)

[View all exhibitions](https://heard.org/exhibitions)

### Membership Has Its Benefits

Your membership to the Heard pays for itself in as little as two visits. Enjoy free museum admission, discounts for events, the Museum Shop and the Courtyard Café, invitations to members-only events and more.

[Join today](https://heard.org/support__trashed/benefits/)

### Stories

[View all stories](https://heard.org/learn/stories)

 [**Making Moccasins at Cochise Stronghold**\\ \\ The Heard Museum’s Master Artist Workshop series held a four-day moccasin-making workshop at Cochise Stronghold in southeastern Arizona with 15 Chiricahua descendants from Mescalero, New Mexico.](https://heard.org/cochise-moccasins/)

 [**Central California Basket Making with Artist Collaborators Monique Sonoquie & Jilli Oyenque**\\ \\ This short film highlights a unique basketry class connecting familiar and new weaving materials with traditional techniques on Chumash lands in central California.](https://heard.org/california-basket-making/)

## Current Temporary Exhibitions

[Four Stories at Pikilyi, by Michael Jagamara Nelson.](https://www.ou.edu/content/fjjma/exhibitions/current-exhibitions/from-the-australian-desert)

October 16, 2026 through March 14, 2027

[**From the Australian Desert**](https://www.ou.edu/content/fjjma/exhibitions/current-exhibitions/from-the-australian-desert)

Fifty years ago, a painting movement emerged at Papunya in Aus­tralia’s Central Desert. It arose with such force and convic­tion that one could be forgiven for thinking it had existed forever, as though etched from the earth by the slow pas­sage of time. In fact, formed in the aftermath of colonization, the enduring art movement is as much a product of recent his­torical circumstances as the ancient traditions on which it draws.

[**Read more** From the Australian Desert](https://www.ou.edu/content/fjjma/exhibitions/current-exhibitions/from-the-australian-desert)

[Various pieces of pottery from the Frankoma Pottery Exhibition.](https://www.ou.edu/content/fjjma/exhibitions/current-exhibitions/frankoma-pottery)

Ongoing

[**Frankoma Pottery**](https://www.ou.edu/content/fjjma/exhibitions/current-exhibitions/frankoma-pottery)

Established in Norman by John Frank in 1933, the Frankoma Pottery Company created art that was “both useful and beautiful” and that remains sought after by collectors today in Oklahoma and beyond. This exhibition celebrates a gift from architects Rodolfo Machado and Jorge Silvetti to the Fred Jones Jr. Museum of Art of over 200 iconic pieces of dinnerware and fine art ceramics, showcasing the innovation and craftsmanship of the state’s first commercial pottery manufacturer. The collection illustrates the Frankoma commitment to producing high-quality objects that exemplify its slogan: “for those who like nice things.”

[**Read more** Frankoma Pottery](https://www.ou.edu/content/fjjma/exhibitions/current-exhibitions/frankoma-pottery)

## About the Museum

The Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art at Cornell University opened in 1973 and has always been open to all without charge. Designed by I. M. Pei & Partners, the Museum is named for Herbert F. Johnson, Class of 1922.

## Land Acknowledgment

Cornell University is located on the traditional homelands of the Gayogo̱hó:nǫɁ (the Cayuga Nation). The Gayogo̱hó:nǫɁ are members of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy, an alliance of six sovereign Nations with a historic and contemporary presence on this land. The Confederacy precedes the establishment of Cornell University, New York state, and the United States of America. We acknowledge the painful history of Gayogo̱hó:nǫɁ dispossession, and honor the ongoing connection of Gayogo̱hó:nǫɁ people, past and present, to these lands and waters.

This land acknowledgment has been reviewed and approved by the traditional Gayogo̱hó:nǫɁ leadership.

# _Giants: Art from the Dean Collection of Swizz Beatz and Alicia Keys_ presented by JPMorganChase

_Giants: Art from the Dean Collection of Swizz Beatz and Alicia Keys_ traces the evolution of an ambitious collection built by musical and cultural icons Kasseem Dean (aka Swizz Beatz) and Alicia Keys over two decades. The exhibition showcases a focused selection of approximately 130 objects from the couple's world-class holdings, spotlighting works by Black diasporic artists in an ongoing effort to expand the art-historical narrative.

[LEARN MORE](https://discovernewfields.org/events-exhibitions/giants-art-from-the-dean-collection-of-swizz-beatz-and-alicia-keys)

# Vote for Newfields in USA Today's 10Best Readers Choice Awards

The USA TODAY 10BEST Readers’ Choice Awards highlight top-notch attractions and businesses, providing readers with trusted recommendations.

You're able to cast your vote one time for each category per day. Come back every morning, and vote to help our institution capture this achievement!

# [Art](https://www.hrm.org/exhibitions/exquisite-creatures/), [Science](https://www.hrm.org/planetarium/), [History](https://www.hrm.org/glenview/)

## Glenview Historic Home

Glenview is an 1877 Gilded Age home on the National Register of Historic Places, designed by architect Charles W. Clinton.

[Guided tours & info →](https://www.hrm.org/glenview/)

[History](https://www.hrm.org/glenview/)

## Planetarium

From the mysteries of the moon and the search for life beyond Earth, to the stories that shape our stars, our Planetarium has shows for every level and interest.

[Planetarium shows & info →](http://www.hrm.org/planetarium)

[Science](https://www.hrm.org/planetarium/)

## Exquisite Creatures

On view through January 31, 2027

[All exhibitions →](https://www.hrm.org/exhibitions/)

[Art](https://www.hrm.org/exhibitions/exquisite-creatures/)

## What’s New

### Diwali Festival 2026

_Saturday, November 14, 2026, 11am–5pm_

Celebrate Diwali, the festival of lights, at the HRM! Make your own _diya_ to take home, create colorful patterns with _rangoli_, the traditional Indian folk art of welcome, learn to drape a sari, get a henna design, and more. Enjoy classical Indian music and interactive dance performances, and learn some Bollywood moves yourself.

[Learn more →](https://www.hrm.org/events/diwali/)

### Holiday Kick-Off

_Friday, November 27, 11am–5pm_ 
_Saturday, November 28, 11am–5pm_ 
_Sunday, November 29, 11am–5pm_

Celebrate the start of the holiday season at the HRM with festive programs all weekend! Don’t miss the return of Thunderbird American Indian Dancers on Friday, and Jim Keyes’ Gallery Performance and Songwriting on Saturday. _This program is supported in part with funding provided by the Westchester Delegation of the New York State Assembly and Senate, and Assemblymember Nader J. Sayegh. Support provided by Art Bridges._

[Learn more →](https://www.hrm.org/events/holiday-kick-off/)

### Bloomberg Connects

Explore the HRM’s digital guide on Bloomberg Connects, the free arts and culture app created by Bloomberg Philanthropies. The guide enhances on-site visits, supports off-site visits, and features exclusive multimedia content that offers new insights about collection and exhibition highlights.

[Learn more →](https://www.hrm.org/explore-the-hrm-with-bloomberg-connects/)

metadata.title: Honolulu Museum of Art
metadata.description: HoMA is a gathering place where art, education and community converge in two iconic buildings in the heart of Honolulu. Presenting our remarkable collection and innovative exhibitions in the galleries, screening the best in new cinema, and offering a full curriculum of studio art classes, HoMA is a vital, transformative part of Hawai‘i’s cultural landscape accessible to all.

# Escape the Ordinary at the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum

In 1903, Isabella Stewart Gardner opened her museum “for the education and enjoyment of the public forever.”

Today's Hours: 10am – 5pm All hours

[Plan Your Visit](https://www.gardnermuseum.org/visit) [Get Tickets](https://tnew.gardnermuseum.org/events)

## Exhibitions

## Now On View

_The Book of Esther in the Age of Rembrandt_ illuminates how the ancient story of a Jewish heroine became a source of inspiration for people across faiths in the 17th-century Netherlands. 

[Learn More](https://www.gardnermuseum.org/exhibitions)

## In the spotlight

Blog

### [A Chorus of Stitches: Isabella Stewart Gardner’s Historic Lace Collection](https://www.gardnermuseum.org/blog/chorus-stitches-isabella-stewart-gardners-historic-lace-collection)

Isabella Stewart Gardner once paid the modern equivalent of $114,500 for a single lace flounce. Historian and lacemaker Elena Kanagy-Loux explores what Isabella’s collection reveals about the booming lace market in the 1800s and the extraordinary skill and labor of the women and girls behind the craft.

November 13–15, 2026

### Member Appreciation Weekend

Join us this weekend as we say thank you to our members with special perks.

[Get Tickets](https://tnew.gardnermuseum.org/37665/38396)

November 15, 2026

### Lysander Piano Trio Weekend Concert

The terrific Lysander Trio, formed when they were students at Juilliard, are phenomenal chamber musicians. 

[More Information](https://www.gardnermuseum.org/calendar/lysander-piano-trio-20261115)

November 16, 2026

### Botanical Talk & Tour

Join a member of the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum horticulture staff for a presentation about the role of plants at the Museum, past and present, followed by an hour-long guided experience through the galleries.

[Get Tickets](https://tnew.gardnermuseum.org/overview/37326)

 ## What's On View

 [Selections from the Collection](https://www.eastman.org/selections-collection-1)

 _Selections from the Collection_ features objects from the museum’s photography and related technology collections. A conceptual thread connects objects, which rotate in and out of the exhibition, to the various lineages that exist throughout the history of photography. Showcased is a field richly interdependent on community networks for its progress.

metadata.description: The George Eastman Museum is located in Rochester, New York, on the estate of George Eastman, the pioneer of popular photography and motion picture film. Founded in 1947 as an independent nonprofit institution, it is the world’s oldest photography museum and one of the oldest film archives.

**The Joslyn**—5,000 years of human creativity in art across three buildings. Free general admission to all, always—generously provided by the Holland Foundation.

The Joslyn is a 2025 & 2026 winner of the USA Today 10Best Readers’ Choice Award for **[Best Art Museum](https://10best.usatoday.com/awards/joslyn-art-museum-omaha-nebraska/)** in the nation and the recipient of the 2026 Omaha Metropolitan Area Tourism Award for **Best Attraction** in Douglas County.

**Hours:** Tue–Sun, 10 am to 4 pm; late until 8 pm on Thu. Closed Mon.

## The Phillip G. Schrager Collection

The inaugural presentation of the collection at The Joslyn celebrates Schrager’s vision and passion for collecting and offers a sweeping perspective on five decades of art.

**Pictured:** Matthew Ritchie (British, b. 1964), _The First Sea,_ 2003, oil and marker on canvas, 99 × 110 in. (251.5 × 279.4 cm), The Phillip G. Schrager Collection. Promised gift of Terri L. Schrager, © Matthew Ritchie, Photograph © Bill Ganzel, Ganzel Group Communications, Inc.

event.name: Made in USA: Prints for the American Revolution Bicentennial
event.description: Hawks Pavilion Works on Paper Gallery H5 What does history look like? In prints commissioned on the occasion of the American Revolution Bicentennial of 1976, artists referenced and remixed familiar icons and narratives, spotlighting the ways ​national history is constructed, communicated, and consumed.

event.name: Café Society: Art and Sociability in Paris, 1855–1914
event.description: Scott Pavilion Galleries S1–3 From bistros and brasseries to cafés-concerts, dance halls, and cabarets, the cafés of Paris were important sites for artistic dialogue, expression, and experimentation. This exhibition considers the development of the French café and its impact on modern art in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

event.description: Hawks Pavilion Media Gallery H6 Jacolby Satterwhite’s intricate digital videos combine performance, animation, and found images to generate self-contained worlds that are at once illusory and grounded in lived experience. For this dreamlike work, Satterwhite used 3D graphics software to revisit a home movie from his childhood.

event.name: Sadie Barnette
event.description: Scott Pavilion Riley CAP Gallery S8 Working across media , Sadie Barnette mines both personal narratives and collective histories, exploring how the two continually intersect and diverge. Her exhibition in the CAP Gallery considers how seemingly unremarkable moments from everyday life may be seen as profound .

## Join us this fall!

[**Block Cinema at 25: Projecting the Future**\\ \\ Throughout the 2026–27 academic year, The Block Museum of Art will celebrate the twenty-fifth anniversary of Block Cinema through a series of screenings, performances, research initiatives, and student-led programs that explore the evolving possibilities of the moving image.\\ \\ Learn More](https://www.blockmuseum.northwestern.edu/projects/block-cinema-at-25-projecting-the-future.html)

## About the Lowe Art Museum

### About the Lowe Art Museum

From its origins in three classrooms in 1950, the Lowe Art Museum has grown into a leading cultural institution. Its history reflects a steadfast commitment to its dual mission: to serve the University of Miami as an essential teaching resource and to enrich the lives of Greater Miami’s residents and visitors as the region’s premier general art museum.

[Learn More](https://www.lowe.miami.edu/visit-about/history/index.html)

## More Details

### Explore the Lowe

As an integral part of the University of Miami, the Lowe Art Museum invites you to engage with over 5,000 years of human creativity. From ancient artifacts to contemporary works, our diverse collections and dynamic exhibitions offer meaningful connections to art and culture across time and place. Whether you're exploring what's on view, joining our community, or discovering new perspectives, the Lowe is your gateway to inspiration.

openGraph.description: The Lowe Art Museum, in Coral Gables, a Miami suburb in Miami-Dade County, is a visual arts museum. It opened in 1950 and is operated by the University of Miami. It was originally established by a gift from philanthropists Joe and Emily Lowe. An integral part of the University of Miami, the Lowe Art Museum offers its diverse audiences opportunities and resources for engaging with contemporary culture through 5,000 years of human creativity.

twitter.imageAlt: image of exterior of the Lowe Art Museum. Showing entrance, white rounded facade with low slung roof that creates a overhang canopy. roof is covered in aluminum. To the right is the Palley Pavillion. A distinctively different architecture style, rectangular modern glass and masonory building. The front of both sections has a series of royal palms.

7,000 years of art from around the world in Rochester, New York

## Haudenosaunee Heritage at MAG

Join us for Haudenosaunee Heritage Celebration Day on Sunday, November 22! Enjoy free museum admission, live dances and demonstrations, storytelling, hands-on activities, display tables, and more.

[Learn more](https://mag.rochester.edu/event/haudenosaunee-heritage-celebration-day/)

## Explore MAG with our digital guide

The mobile guide offers access to new perspectives on highlights from MAG’s permanent collection, grounds, and temporary exhibitions, including a new tour of the evolution of perspective in artwork by MAG member Forrest Hurlbut.

[Learn more](https://mag.rochester.edu/visit/digital-guide/)

## Bring a group to MAG

Interested in visiting the MAG with a group of ten or more people? We offer self-guided visits and guided tours of the collection and/or our special exhibitions for adult, youth, and college groups.

[Learn more about group experiences](https://mag.rochester.edu/visit/group-experiences/)

## Free for All, _Forever_

Fueled by more than $9 million in community support, the _Free for All, Forever_ initiative will make general admission free for everyone starting on May 1, 2027, and sustain access to art and culture for generations to come.

[Learn more about this initiative](https://mag.rochester.edu/free/)

### ON VIEW

## _Memphis College of Art, 1936-2020: An Enduring Legacy 
_

In May of 2020, the Memphis College of Art (MCA) graduated its last class of students, ending an illustrious 84-year history of contributing to the creative, economic, and cultural flourishing of the city of Memphis. In addition to being a touchstone for the regional arts community, MCA graduates ventured across the country and around the world where they nurtured their own careers as well as inspired generations of others through teaching. The college’s history is intimately tied not only to the city but also to the Brooks Memorial Art Gallery, today the Memphis Brooks Museum of Art.

[Learn More](https://www.brooksmuseum.org/exhibitions/mca-at-memphis-brooks-museum-of-art)

**_Jill Wissmiller, The Gilding of Lily, 2011_**

### on view

## _Navigating Knowledge 
_

This exhibition explores vessels and navigation as metaphors for the containment and transmission of knowledge. From religious doctrine and scientific theories to historical narratives and ancient philosophies, the works presented consider how ideas spread to the far reaches of the world through migration and other journeys. 

Harmonia Rosales, _Migration of the Gods_, 2021 

[Learn More](https://www.brooksmuseum.org/exhibitions/navigating-knowledge)

### new exhibition | now on view

## _David Uzochukwu: Bodies of Water 
_

David Uzochukwu: Bodies of Water is a poetic meditation on identity, migration, and belonging. In his first solo museum exhibition, Uzochukwu presents hybrid beings—part human, part animal—who inhabit surreal, dreamlike landscapes. His use of nonhuman features amplifies, rather than diminishes, the strength and dignity of his subjects.

[Learn More](https://www.brooksmuseum.org/exhibitions/david-uzochukwu-bodies-of-water)

_David Uzochukwu, 'Shrine', 2019_

##### Land Acknowledgement

Kemper Museum of Contemporary Art acknowledges it resides on the ancestral territory of the Osage, Kaw, and Otoe-Missouria, among other tribal nations forcibly moved to the region such as the Shawnee, Wyandot, Delaware, Potawatomi, Sac and Fox and Kiikaapoi (Kickapoo) nations. We recognize and support the continued vibrancy of Native communities and cultures today who continue to thrive, as well as the inherent sovereignty of tribal nations. We are compelled to serve and advocate for these communities in accordance with our public mission.

Kemper Museum acknowledges and respects the diversity of Native people connected to this land today. Many recognize the land and all beings who live within it as relatives. We acknowledge the earth we inhabit, the waters of the Blue River, the Kansas River, the Missouri River, and the plants, animals, and people supported by them.

We acknowledge our responsibility to be good caretakers of the land we occupy.

[Click here to learn more about our land acknowledgment process.](https://www.kemperart.org/land-acknowledgement)

 A photograph can be many things: a portrait, a document, a love token. ❤️ 

 Born on this day in 1826, Charles Hugo created this daguerreotype of his father, Victor Hugo, writing at his desk. 

 Victor gifted the unique photograph to Juliette Drouet with a poem he wrote, transforming the image into a deeply personal keepsake: 

 “When I am no more than chilly ash, 
 My weary eyes closed to the sky above, 
 Say to yourself, my image fixed in your heart: The world has 
 his thoughts; 
 I had his love.” 

 See this work in “Photography’s First Century: Masterworks from the Bibliothèque nationale de France”: kimbellart.org/photography

 Can you spot the signature that caused a famous mix-up? 👀 

 When “La Pointe de la Hève at Low Tide” (1865) was exhibited at the Paris Salon, some viewers mistook Claude Monet's signature for that of the more established Édouard Manet. 

 After receiving praise for a painting that wasn't his, Manet sought out Monet, beginning one of the most significant artistic friendships of the 19th century. 

 This beach scene near Le Havre, where Monet grew up, was one of two landscapes that helped launch his career. 🌊 

 In honor of Monet, born on this day in 1840, see this work on view in the north gallery of the Kahn Building.

jsonLd.name: Meadows Museum, SMU Dallas
jsonLd.description: The Meadows Museum is the leading U.S. institution focused on the study and presentation of the art of Spain. In 1962, Dallas businessman and philanthropist Algur H. Meadows donated his private collection of Spanish paintings, as well as funds to start a museum, to Southern Methodist University. The Museum opened to the public in 1965, marking the first step in fulfilling Meadows’s vision to create “a small Prado for Texas.” Today, the Meadows is home to one of the largest and most comprehensive collections of Spanish art outside of Spain. The collection spans from the 10th to the 21st centuries and includes medieval objects, Renaissance and Baroque sculptures, and major paintings by Golden Age and modern masters.
openingHours: Closed on Mondays, Easter Sunday, July 4, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and New Year’s Day.

address.streetAddress: 5900 Bishop Blvd., Dallas, TX 75205  P.O. Box 750357

jsonLd.headline: Meadows Museum
jsonLd.description: The Meadows Museum’s vision is to be the leading center in the United States for exhibition, research and education in the arts and culture of Spain. The Meadows Museum, a division of the Meadows School of the Arts at Southern Methodist University (SMU), advances knowledge, understanding and appreciation of the arts and culture of Spain through the collection and interpretation of works of the greatest aesthetic and historical importance.

Background video description: Various vignettes of the Milwaukee Art Museum campus experience show what it’s like to visit and what guests can expect to see throughout the space—from the white, modern Calatrava building facing Lake Michigan, a child eagerly running toward the entrance off of the Reiman Bridge, and a guest taking in the expanse of Windover Hall to a group of friends enjoying the East Lawn off Oak Leaf Trail, a parent and a child enjoying art in a gallery together, and children painting under a teacher’s instruction at the Art studio.

# Welcome to New York City’s most iconic museum.

[Buy tickets](https://engage.metmuseum.org/admission/?promocode=65436) [Plan your visit](https://www.metmuseum.org/visit/plan-your-visit)

---

##### General Admission: $30

Pay-what-you-wish for NY residents. Free for Members and children 12 and under. 

##### On Manhattan’s Upper East Side

Take the 4/5/6 subway lines or M1, M2, M3, M4, M79, or M86 bus. 

##### Free guided tours in ten languages

Check our [tour schedule](https://www.metmuseum.org/tours) for times.

##### Open today 10 am–5 pm

Closed on Wednesdays.

### Become a Member

Enjoy an enhanced experience with unlimited free admission, special access to exhibitions, and invitations to Members-only events.

[Join today](https://engage.metmuseum.org/members/membership/?promocode=65700)

##### Free admission

For you and at least one guest

##### Express entry

Via the Members Entrance at 81st Street

##### Member Preview Days

Preview exhibitions before they open to the public

##### Discounts on shopping, dining, and parking

Enjoy ongoing deals and special seasonal offers

#### Native American and Indigenous Heritage Month

Celebrate the rich culture and history of Native American and Indigenous communities through art, talks, and more.

[Learn more](https://www.metmuseum.org/cultural-heritage-months-and-holidays/native-american-and-indigenous-heritage-month)

#### Holidays at The Met

Celebrate the season with festive decorations, world-famous artwork, live performances, holiday treats, and more.

[Explore now](https://www.metmuseum.org/hubs/holidays-at-the-met)

#### Your Members-only mini tote awaits!

Become a Member by December 31 to claim your limited-edition mini tote.

[Join today](https://engage.metmuseum.org/members/join?promocode=66350)

#### Holiday Gifting

Plan ahead for the holiday season with new and best-selling designs inspired by The Met collection.

[Shop The Met Store](https://store.metmuseum.org/)

The Mildred Lane Kemper Art Museum is free and open to the public. Its mission is to collect significant modern and contemporary art and preserve its collection for current and future generations; provide excellence in art historical research, exhibition, and object-based learning; and engage the campus population, its visitors and alumni, the St. Louis region, and the global art community.

## New Gallery Space and Updated Study Center

### Now Open!

Our renovation of administrative spaces into 3,600 new square feet of exhibition space and updated 1,000 square-foot-Bishop Study Center opened on October 27. This renovation will allow visitors to immediately be greeted by art upon their arrival. The first exhibition in the new gallery space is a presentation of The Florida Art Collection, which is a recent gift of 1,200 works of Florida-themed art given by Samuel H. and Roberta T. Vickers. The renovation is a partnership with UF’s Planning, Design and Construction team; an integrated design firm, DLR Group; and the general contractor, Scorpio Construction.

[Learn More](https://harn.ufl.edu/news/harn-museum-of-art-opens-year-long-renovation-project-on-oct-27-featuring-a-new-art-gallery-and-upgraded-study-center/)

SUPPORT THE HARN Annual Fund

## Invest in a Museum for Students, Community and the World!

Annual Fund gifts support free admission and make our exhibitions, programs, and teaching opportunities possible. Because of you, the Harn remains open and accessible to all. Every contribution, no matter the size, has a meaningful impact.

[make a gift](https://giving.uff.ufl.edu/giving-opportunities/016131-harn-annual-fund/)

Our Mission & Vision

## Inspiring, educating and enriching people’s lives through art

The Harn uses the power of the visual arts to open conversations about our shared cultural history and pressing contemporary issues through exhibitions, collections, scholarship and programming of the highest caliber.

# Paris Couture

# Now Open!

Experience luxury up close and watch it evolve through the 20th century. Moving from the glamour of early couture to its golden mid-century peak and into the present, you’ll see how Paris designers turned dressmaking into high art—and how the idea of luxury keeps transforming in our own time.

[Learn More](https://new.artsmia.org/exhibition/paris-couture)
